PullRequest.Title: sessions: refactor: build the sessions list model in a pure function
PullRequest.Body:
### Agent assessment Self-reported assessment, not an independent review. Assessed revision: `af880f46dd2cc5ad0735460e1d6c288edf4309e8` | Dimension | Assessment | Rationale | |---|---|---| | Change confidence | 9.5/10 | ↑ All 53 CI checks on `af880f46dd2` passed (`Compile & Hygiene`, Linux/Windows Electron-Unit and Browser-Unit, Linux Electron-Smoke shards 1-3, Linux Browser, Linux Remote integration/smoke, Playwright Fixture Tests, Screenshots & Tests, CodeQL, Telemetry, PR Gate) and `dmitrivMS` approved.
↑ Local `typecheck-client`, `oxlint` (8 files), `valid-layers-check`, `check-cyclic-dependencies` (12,100 files), and 841 targeted sessions-list unit tests passed.
↑ Line-by-line semantic audit of `origin/main` vs `HEAD` confirmed parity for `#350603` scoping, `#350669` pinned headers, and non-boolean collapse-state filtering; live Code OSS Agents-window testing verified both `sessions.sidebar.separateNavigation` layouts (`false` and `true`), session and custom-group pin/unpin, Find filter/restore, and grouping switches with zero page or console errors.
↓ Direct DOM-free unit tests in `sessionsListModel.test.ts` cover 7 scenarios (relying on `sessionsList.test.ts` and CI for remaining edge cases), and live testing did not exercise multi-workspace `"+N more"` capping or Inbox mode with populated attention items. | ### Why `SessionsList` previously built its tree nodes inline while mutating scattered render-state fields, writing legacy collapse-key migrations to storage, and logging setting experiment triggers mid-render. Extracting model construction into a pure function separates data derivation from widget side effects and allows testing list grouping, capping, ordering, Inbox transitions, scoping, pinned headers, and comparison attachment without a DOM or workbench harness. ### What changed - **Pure model builder (`sessionsListModel.ts`)**: Added `buildSessionsListModel()` and `filterSessionsForList()`, which accept an explicit `ISessionsListModelInput` (including `now`, `scoped`, `hasSessionScope`, `scopeBar`, `isSessionInScope`, and `pinnedSectionIds`) and return tree children, separate navigation sections, filtered sessions, an immutable `ISessionsListRenderSnapshot` (including `renderedPinnedHeaderIds`), deferred `migratedCollapseStateKeys`, and experiment `triggers`. - **Widget integration (`sessionsList.ts`)**: Replaced inline tree assembly and mutable per-render maps/sets with a single `_renderSnapshot` updated in `applyModelResult()`, where storage migrations, experiment triggers, navigation sections, and `tree.setChildren()` are applied. Inbox mode continues to reactively observe `computeInboxPlacements()` over `filterSessionsForList()` and passes the precomputed result into `buildSessionsListModel()`. Preserves list-side `sessionScope`, `pendingSessionScope`, and `scopeBar` behavior from #350603, pinned custom groups and grouping sections from #350669, and filters non-boolean entries when constructing `savedSectionCollapseState`. - **Deterministic helpers & layering (`sessionsListHelpers.ts`, `sessionsListCommon.ts`, `sessionsListDragAndDrop.ts`, `sessionsListRenderers.ts`)**: Threaded optional `nowMs` through `groupSessionsForList`, `groupByDate`, and `partitionByDate`; moved `SessionGroupConnectorPosition` to `sessionsListCommon.ts` and `keepDateSectionOrder` to `sessionsListHelpers.ts` so the pure model has no UI/DnD dependency. - **Unit tests (`sessionsListModel.test.ts`, `sessionsList.test.ts`)**: Added 7 DOM-free unit tests in `sessionsListModel.test.ts` covering workspace folder capping, Date grouping and next time-boundary calculation, Inbox placements and Working-section collapse transitions, non-mutating legacy collapse-key migrations/experiment triggers, comparison group attachment, `scopeBar` / list-side session scoping, and pinned groups/sections; added a regression test in `sessionsList.test.ts` for ignoring non-boolean saved collapse-state entries. ### Validation - `pnpm run build-fast` - passed (client, extensions, copilot) - `pnpm run typecheck-client` - passed (0 errors) - `pnpm run oxlint` on all 8 changed files - passed (0 errors/warnings) - `pnpm run valid-layers-check` and `pnpm run check-cyclic-dependencies` (12,100 files) - passed - `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/views/sessionsListModel.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsArchiveActions.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsListContextMenu.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsListModelService.test.ts` - 841 passing - Live Code OSS Agents-window verification: verified both `sessions.sidebar.separateNavigation` layouts (`false` and `true`), live session and custom-group creation + pin/unpin, Find filter/restore, and grouping switches (`Time`, `Workspace`, `Repository`, `Environment`) with zero renderer/page errors - GitHub CI on `af880f46dd2`: all 53 checks green (Electron/Browser unit tests on Linux & Windows, Electron smoke shards 1-3, Playwright Fixture Tests, Screenshots & Tests, Compile & Hygiene, CodeQL, Telemetry, PR Gate)

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Every rendered non-shortcut section or custom group called getSavedCollapseState, which reparsed the entire persisted collapse-state JSON object. With H rendered headers and K saved keys, repeated list updates performed O(H*K) deserialization/allocation even though storage.get itself is an in-memory cache lookup.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Statically established synchronous CPU and allocation amplification when rendering many workspace/custom-group headers, especially with Show All Sessions or active search and a large persisted collapse-state map; no measured timings are claimed.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: sessionsList.ts:1832 reads/parses and converts collapse state once per update; the model's getSavedCollapseState uses Map.get for each header, reducing normal reads to O(K+H). Legacy migrations lazily copy once and applyModelResult writes the combined migrations once rather than serializing per migrated header.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Deleted renderSection and renderGroup implementations in sessionsList.ts call this.getSavedCollapseState for each emitted header. The unchanged helper's base line 6301 executes JSON.parse(raw), and blame resolves that line to the introducing commit. Added sessionsList.ts:1832 builds one input map; sessionsListModel.ts:767-770 selects that map and performs source.get(sectionId), reused by renderSection and renderGroup. update is reached synchronously by filters/group/pin changes and by coalesced animation-frame metadata updates. Storage.get is cache-backed (base/parts/storage/common/storage.ts:218-219), so the removed cost is repeated deserialization, not one filesystem read per header.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or rebuild session history in Date, Workspace, Repository, or Environment grouping; change scope, pinning, custom groups, ordering, or show-more caps.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Filtering, sorting, group/comparison construction, collapse-state lookup, comparison attachment, and tree.setChildren complete synchronously before updated rows are usable. The extracted builder preserves the existing collection scans and caps. Persistence flushes remain asynchronous.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse persisted collapse-state JSON and convert valid entries into a lookup map.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full parse/map construction per update; each of H headers then uses Map.get. A migration additionally reads the state once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each rendered non-shortcut section or custom group independently parsed all K saved entries through getSavedCollapseState, producing O(H*K) deserialization rather than O(K+H).

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist legacy collapse-key migrations through cached profile storage and a delayed batched database update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One combined store for all migrations in a rebuild, zero without migrations. Storage pendingInserts coalesces changes by key before the delayed database flush.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One serialization/store per migrated header; database operations were already delayed and coalesced, so there was not necessarily one database call per header.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Stringification/cache update is synchronous; database flush is not awaited by list rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N listed sessions and their nested chats, G custom groups, comparison participants, H actually rendered headers, and K saved collapse keys. Folder and session caps reduce rendered rows but do not eliminate inventory filtering/sorting.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model construction and tree application are synchronous and serial. Metadata/host changes coalesce through scheduleListUpdate's animation-frame slot; additions/removals and user group/filter/pin changes retain their existing synchronous updates. Storage flush uses a ThrottledDelayer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Storage reads are in-memory string-cache lookups, not filesystem reads per header. Collapse state is rebuilt once per update, preserving external-window changes. Derived attention is already kept observed by SessionsListModelService's autorun, so the newly unconditional attention.get does not initiate a fresh whole-history attention computation per ordinary render.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: complete before/after hunks, update callers, collapse helper, and cache-backed storage implementation establish the cost reduction. Blame provenance was collected and the concrete fix recorded internally.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings or production history-size distributions are available; large H and K clearly amplify the old parse cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced regression. The PR removes repeated full collapse-state deserialization and batches migration serialization; other collection-wide work is moved rather than newly added.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display Inbox and react to attention/status/order updates.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The visible list filters once, synchronously computes observed placements, builds the model, and applies tree children. Chat hydration and GitHub refresh/polling supply later attention updates but are not awaited before initial rows render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh/poll PR metadata and reviews, with optional review-thread and CI models for assigned open PRs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A cold PR model refresh issues metadata and review operations per distinct owner/repo/PR key; assigned open PRs add review-thread and head-keyed CI refreshes. Endpoint pagination may increase HTTP calls. Shared references and the WeakSet prevent fresh refreshes for every session or list rebuild.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same updateInboxDemand acquired attention, and the same service performed keyed refreshes/polling. The old list autorun read the same attention map.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background operations are not awaited by buildSessionsListModel or tree.setChildren; later results may trigger coalesced placement updates.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire/load provider-backed chat models for NeedsInput notifications, potentially crossing provider IPC/network/filesystem boundaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one outstanding load per distinct missing chat resource; loaded models, retained references, in-flight maps, and unavailable-provider tracking suppress redundant loads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical service-owned chat loading and cancellation before the extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Loads are launched asynchronously and are not awaited by the list builder; hydration can update attention afterward.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F filtered sessions for placement maps; service tracking can cover all eligible sessions. Remote multiplicity is controlled by distinct PR keys, assigned PRs with open heads, and distinct unloaded NeedsInput chat resources, not one request per visible row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One replaceable Inbox autorun per list and an animation-frame update slot. Independent PR models run concurrently, while the GitHub request queue has bounded admission/concurrency (defaults 12 total/host, 10 account, 8 caller). Chat loads are deduplicated per resource rather than globally limited at the attention-service layer; this is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The precomputedInbox argument reuses the filtering result and initial placement map rather than filtering/computing twice. Placement equality avoids tree rebuilds when attention changes without moving a placement/order. PR references are keyed and refresh promises join same-priority in-flight work; CI keys include head SHA. Chat loads are keyed and canceled/released when inactive.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both old and new autoruns, precomputed filtering, service ownership, reference keys, refresh joining, and request-queue limits were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: PR endpoint pagination, remote latency, chat-provider costs, and eligible-history size vary; no measured durations are available.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced fan-out, concurrency burst, duplicate filtering, or lost coalescing. Remote work and demand ownership remain unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type Find queries and restore normal capped/collapsed layout afterward, including comparison attachments.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Search-triggered rebuilds construct searchable metadata, filter Inbox sections/eligible comparison callers, and update the tree synchronously. Existing non-Inbox query changes without attached comparisons can remain tree-filter-only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/parse collapse state when the query requires a full model rebuild.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per model rebuild rather than once per expanded rendered header; no extra provider request is required for searchable metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Search already bypassed caps and expanded rows, with repeated per-header collapse-state parsing during rebuilds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous CPU before tree update; profile storage retrieval itself is cache-backed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Sessions and chats exposed while search bypasses caps, rendered tree size, comparison callers, and query frequency. Effective matching cardinality is one match/document per session object per invalidation, reused by the tree filter.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous search matching/tree application; existing pattern-change conditions determine full rebuilds. No new async task or expensive external call was added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: searchFilter.invalidate still resets matches for a rebuild. getMatchForSession and getMatch use the same session-keyed map with null negative caching, so matching before tree application is reused afterward. Collapse restoration consumes the same saved snapshot; comparison data is render-local rather than re-fetched.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: search filter methods, pattern listeners, explicit search-document context, and before/after comparison attachment were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large histories and long searchable chat titles affect synchronous matching time, but their traversal and uncapping existed before this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence regression. Richer explicit metadata does not increase matching frequency or invalidate the existing negative/positive match cache.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show separate navigation/canvases, collapse navigation, hide and re-show the sidebar, or dispose the list.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Navigation section comparison, any necessary splice/layout, and tree application are synchronous. Re-show skips non-Inbox rebuilds unless hidden data changed or the existing time-validity deadline expired.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Pinned canvas entries, rendered groups/rows, and one latest render snapshot per list. The new eager pinned-canvas section mapping can run even while its navigation header is collapsed, but it only constructs lightweight metadata from cached entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DOM work remains serial on the renderer thread. MutableDisposable owns replaceable observers and scheduled callbacks; existing list disposal owns cleanup. No new process, network request, or heavyweight canvas initialization is started by section mapping.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: setNavigationSections retains its equality check and avoids unchanged splices/layout. The render snapshot replaces prior maps/sets rather than accumulating versions. Hiding clears the Inbox observer and demand; the latest placement map remains bounded by that last rendered inventory. Time-sensitive validity computation and hidden-refresh conditions are preserved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged layout suppression and lifecycle ownership; insufficient evidence that the small eager metadata work constitutes an actionable regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Canvas counts and retained last-Inbox placement-map size are unknown; inspected additions are bounded lightweight metadata, without evidence of significant user-visible degradation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable synchronous-layout or retention regression. Existing geometry/layout calls are not newly added or multiplied.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand Done/archived history and load cloud archived sessions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The model may emit the Done header and immediately apply it. Archive demand is acquired after tree application only when visible, archives are allowed, and Done is expanded; remote history must arrive for those additional sessions to appear, not for the initial tree to render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request archived provider inventory through cloud session discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Provider setRequested(true) occurs only on the shared zero-to-one demand transition. Cold/unloaded or error archive state triggers a discovery refresh; already-loaded successful state does not re-fetch simply because the list rebuilds. Discovery calls serve the provider inventory, with backend pagination as applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same visibility/expanded-Done gate, shared archive request counter, and provider discovery mechanism ran after tree.setChildren.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous after tree application; fetch completion gates additional archived rows but is not awaited by the builder.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Registered archive providers, account/environment inventory, and returned archive pages. Demand fans out by provider, not by each session/header.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One archive demand lease per list, shared reference counting across consumers, and serialized inventory scans per discovery controller; feed-task reads use their existing separate coalescing lane.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reading archivedSessionItems.available is a derived state read, not a request. Discovery retains successful archivesLoaded state and retries cold/error states. Compatible in-flight inventory requests join; incompatible requests coalesce into a queued pass.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: model availability read, post-render demand gate, archive service counter, cloud registration, and discovery cache/in-flight logic were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Archive volume, backend page count, and latency are unmeasured; the diff does not change those multiplicities.
Scenarios.Verdict: No new eager archive fetch, per-session network fan-out, or critical-path await.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all eight changed files and all diff pages. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regressions qualified for report_finding. Recorded one concrete fixed repeated-deserialization mechanism with base-line blame provenance. Review is static; timings and production cardinalities were not measured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
